title: DRAFT: Decoupling Backpropagation from Pre-trained Backbone for Efficient Transformer Fine-Tuning on Edge
problem: Efficient fine-tuning of pre-trained Transformers on resource-constrained edge devices, where backpropagation through massive backbone weights incurs high computational cost and memory overhead.
motivation: Transformer fine-tuning requires expensive backpropagation through pre-trained weights; edge devices with limited compute and memory need efficient alternatives to enable on-device personalization.
method: DRAFT solves the problem of expensive gradient calculations during fine-tuning on edge devices by splitting backpropagation (the process of calculating weight updates) into two separate pathways via Feedback Decoupling Approximation (FDA): a trainable adapter and a sparse ternary Bypass Network (a network using mostly-zero weights to efficiently approximate gradients). Custom hardware—a reconfigurable DRAFT accelerator—runs these pathways by exploiting sparsity (the many zeros) and data parallelism (splitting work across processors) through sparse gather networks and dynamic workflows.
key_novelty: The key innovation is algorithm-hardware co-design (designing a special algorithm and custom hardware together) where Feedback Decoupling Approximation splits backpropagation (gradient calculation) into two lightweight pathways rather than computing through the entire pre-trained model, reducing computational cost while preserving training accuracy.
contributions: FDA algorithm that decouples backpropagation into low-complexity adapter and sparse ternary BPN pathways
DRAFT accelerator with reconfigurable design featuring sparse gather networks
4.9x speedup and 4.2x energy efficiency improvement over baseline fine-tuning methods
Negligible accuracy loss across multiple fine-tuning tasks
primary_theme: Edge-efficient transformer fine-tuning via backpropagation decoupling
